people.name: Philopater
people.description: Ptolemaic king who defeated Antiochus at Raphia, tried to enter the temple, and persecuted then released the Jews of Egypt.
people.identity_note: Ptolemy IV Philopator. Arsinoe is called his sister (1:1); no parents or spouse are stated in 3MA.

people.name: Antiochus
people.description: Seleucid king defeated by Ptolemy IV at Raphia.
people.identity_note: Historically Antiochus III; distinct from Antiochus IV of 2/4MA.

people.name: Arsinoe
people.description: Sister of Ptolemy IV who rallied the troops at Raphia with promises of gold.
people.identity_note: 3MA calls her his sister (1:1); historically Arsinoe III was also his wife, but the text does not say so, so no spouse is recorded.

people.name: Theodotus
people.description: Officer who tried to assassinate Ptolemy in his tent before Raphia.

people.name: Dositheus
people.description: Apostate Jew who saved Ptolemy by placing a substitute in his tent.
people.identity_note: 'Called the son of Drimulus'. Distinct from the Dositheuses of 2MA 12.

people.name: Drimulus
people.description: Father of Dositheus.

people.name: The obscure man in Ptolemy's tent
people.description: Obscure person placed in Ptolemy's bed who was killed in his stead.

people.name: Simon
people.description: High priest who prayed against Ptolemy's intrusion into the sanctuary.
people.identity_note: Historically Simon II (c. 219-196 BCE), probably the Simon son of Onias praised in Sirach 50:1; reviewer should reconcile with the SIR census id. Distinct from the Simons of 2MA.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.description: Pharaoh of the exodus, drowned in the sea with his chariots.
people.identity_note: Mapped to the pharaoh of the plagues and Red Sea crossing.

people.name: Hermon
people.description: Keeper of the king's elephants ordered to drug them for the execution of the Jews.
people.identity_note: Personal name here, not Mount Hermon.

people.name: Phalaris
people.description: Notoriously cruel tyrant (of Acragas) to whom the king is compared.
people.identity_note: Historical non-biblical figure mentioned only by comparison.

people.name: Eleazar
people.description: Aged, illustrious priest of the country whose prayer preceded the deliverance at the hippodrome.
people.identity_note: Different person from Eleazar the martyr of 2MA 6/4MA (different setting: Egypt under Ptolemy IV).

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch; the Jews are called his seed.

people.name: Jacob
people.description: Patriarch; the Jews are called his children and race.

people.name: Sennacherim
people.description: Assyrian king who threatened Jerusalem.

people.name: Hananiah (one of the three friends)
people.description: One of the three friends delivered from the furnace.
people.identity_note: 'The three friends in the land of Babylon' clearly denotes Daniel's companions; unnamed here.

people.name: Mishael (one of the three friends)
people.description: One of the three friends delivered from the furnace.

people.name: Azariah (one of the three friends)
people.description: One of the three friends delivered from the furnace.

people.name: Daniel
people.description: Delivered from the lions.

people.name: Jonah
people.description: Delivered from the sea monster.

notes: Setting: Ptolemy IV Philopator after Raphia (217 BCE). 'The king' throughout = Ptolemy IV; refs list a representative set. Skipped unnamed minor figures: the person who sent the banquet invitations (5:14), the king's financier (6:30), the two angels (6:18, not human). 'Israel' (nation) excluded. No explicit ages. Egyptian-month dates from 6:38 recorded in dated_events (no years). Eleazar here is a different priest from the martyr Eleazar (eleazar-martyr) of 2MA/4MA.

dated_events.event: Registration of the Jews begins (runs to 4 Epiphi, forty days).
Measures for the destruction of the Jews last from 5 to 7 Epiphi.
